items.content: The water holds you differently at night, darker and more deliberate, as though it has been waiting for something exactly your size. Every stroke pulls you deeper into a silence that has nothing to do with sound — the shore behind you dissolving into suggestion, the stars above flattening into a ceiling you will never reach. You are neither falling nor floating but suspended in some third condition the body has no name for, aware, suddenly, of how little separates breathing from not.

items.content: The train announced itself long before it arrived, a low moan threading through the darkness like a needle pulling silk. She lay still beneath the sheets, listening as the sound swelled and then faded, the way certain memories do. It passed through the town without stopping, as it always did, carrying its cargo of elsewhere into the night. She wondered, not for the first time, where a person had to stand to be somewhere worth stopping for.

items.content: The alarm had not yet sounded when she opened her eyes, the room thick with a darkness that felt almost deliberate, as though the world had agreed to hold itself still a little longer. She lay listening to the silence, that rare and fragile kind that exists only before birdsong, before traffic, before the slow machinery of morning begins its turning. Rising, she moved to the window and pressed her palm against the cold glass, watching the street below lie empty and unhurried, belonging entirely to no one.
